subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Japanese Bird Songs, Better Thinking, Magic, and Vocal Percussion

bullets.title: Relaxing Bird Songs and Nature
bullets.note: The location is Ōtaki Village, Kiso District, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. I can’t wait to get back to good ol’ Nihon. [_Natsukashii_](http://www.bbc.com/travel/story/20200119-a-uniquely-japanese-take-on-nostalgia#:~:text=Natsukashii%20is%20a%20Japanese%20word,fond%20memory%20from%20your%20past.&text=But%20natsukashii%20%E2%80%93%20which%20derives%20from,desire%20to%20return%20to%20it.)!

bullets.title: V Shivapriya & BR Somashekar Jois | Konnakkol Duet
bullets.note:
This might just blow your mind, especially if you remember that these vocal gymnastics can be transferred directly to percussion instruments. [Jump to 2:40 for a short preview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=AkxdE85o939yLh4Z&t=160&v=iurhjlBum0o). From the description: “We begin Season 3 with the most traditional, classical & ancient vocal percussive art form of India; the mother of all percussive languages – Konnakkol. In this video, we present to you an exclusive ‘Konnakkol Duet’ by Vidwan B R Somashekar Jois and Kumari V Shivapriya.”  
​  
If you want extra credit, pair this video with a few clips of renowned drummer [Terry Bozzio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Bozzio) ([@TerryBozzio](https://twitter.com/terrybozzio)): “[Solos & Duets](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a3F7ZizBPWg)” (1hr+) and “[Baby Snakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hQtqvl3FsBY)” (three-minute drum solo). Thanks to drummer [Dave Elitch](https://tim.blog/2018/11/26/dave-elitch/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf) ([@daveelitch](https://www.instagram.com/daveelitch/?hl=en)) for all the recommendations.

bullets.title: Derek DelGaudio’s In & Of Itself
bullets.note: (Hulu). Derek’s feats of magic are rivaled by his feats of social engineering, memory, and more. I found the entire show incredibly inventive. Even if you don’t have Hulu or won’t subscribe, [the trailer here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0I8s9OzmHHQ) is worth watching. Description: “Storyteller and conceptual magician Derek DelGaudio attempts to understand the illusory nature of identity and answer the deceptively simple question ‘Who am I?’”
